top_choice_rationale: P001 (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, B014) has the strongest combination of originality, breadth and durability on the shortlist. It credits three separable, identifiable contributions: the tractable pricing friction, staggered contracts with the policy rule, and the welfare-based synthesis. No earlier prize recognised this pricing-friction and policy-rule core. The framework was revised, not abandoned, after 2008, the zero lower bound and the post-2021 inflation. I give the explicit-support count no weight as merit. The main costs are attribution, since Galí, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Evans, Smets, Wouters and Gertler are excluded, and the contested empirical identification of the pricing and policy-rule parameters. A narrowly worded citation naming the three components and not claiming the estimated-DSGE tradition limits the claim without removing the cost. P002 (Kiyotaki-Moore) is a cleanly attributed, distinct mechanism that I rank second, though the original contribution is theoretical and its identification came mostly from later work. No award is ranked last because both proposals are mature, substantial contributions.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no co-authorship or institutional link to Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, Kiyotaki or Moore. Main co-author Magnus Johannesson was a former committee member and I co-authored with former chair Tore Ellingsen in 2009, but neither is a candidate. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
